newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: ARGENTINE GOV'T SEES EASY RIDE FOR MONOPOLY BILL.
newsitem.headline: ARGENTINE GOV'T SEES EASY RIDE FOR MONOPOLY BILL.

text.p: An Argentine anti-monopoly bill enjoys broad support in Congress and should be approved within a month, government officials said Wednesday.
Speaking after a meeting in the Economy Ministry to discuss the bill, Peronist Party congressman Rodolfo Gabrielli said that major parties would give it an easy ride through Congress.
The bill would grant new powers to the Commission to Defend Competition, which depends on the Economy Ministry.
"The Commision to Defend Competition would become an autonomous tribunal with the power to evaluate whether business concentration could effect the function of a market," said Gabrielli.
Industry Secretary Alieto Guadagni said the bill will take into consideration World Trade Organization rules and also the U.S. anti-competition system.
